blinding_guess.why: The trajectory-execution settings are split across two namespaces. The code reads allowed_goal_duration_margin only at ~allowed_goal_duration_margin, and the ~/trajectory_execution dynamic_reconfigure config has no such field. The config template in the same snapshot sets trajectory_execution/allowed_goal_duration_margin, so that value is silently ignored. The value read from ~allowed_execution_duration_scaling is also overwritten by the dynamic_reconfigure callback with the trajectory_execution/ value.

notes: All seven packet elements are ROS 1 parameters, so msg_type, qos, rate and definition_id are null and definition_hash.py was not needed. The code names the four root-level parameters relative to the private NodeHandle("~") (trajectory_execution_manager.cpp:76) and the two trajectory_execution/ parameters relative to NodeHandle("~/trajectory_execution") (:57). They resolve to /move_group/... because moveit_ros_move_group instantiates TrajectoryExecutionManager inside node 'move_group' (move_group_context.cpp:53, node_name.h:44). The node name comes from that other package, so another host node would resolve them elsewhere. declares uses the packet's resolved names so the entries compare consistently across runs. The four root-level parameters are read only by the one-argument constructor (:75-88). The two-argument constructor (:90) takes manage_controllers as an argument and reads none of them. allowed_execution_duration_scaling is read from ~ at construction (:81). The dynamic_reconfigure server is then created in initialize() (:157), and its callback (:67) sets the member from the trajectory_execution/ value (cfg default 1.1). That follows the standard dynamic_reconfigure::Server behaviour of invoking the callback on setCallback, which is library behaviour and was not verified inside the snapshot. The effective value therefore comes from the trajectory_execution/ parameter. The ~/trajectory_execution config also declares execution_velocity_scaling (cfg:8), which is not a packet element. exclusive is empty: the only 'exclusive' in the package is a collision-detector activation flag in collision_plugin_loader, not a resource claim. The manager switches controllers through the MoveItControllerManager plugin but names no exclusive resource tokens. references is empty because every packet element is on the provides side. Units for the two scaling parameters are left null: the code describes them as multiplicative factors and states no unit.
